Evergreen Reflections

memories below

Slow Burn

One August evening, Evergreen Lake had two skies. One hung overhead and the other lay upside down on the water, so still that I couldn't tell where one ended and the other began. A little before eight, the sky was only a pale peach. A line of dark red buoys ran across the lake like a dotted line drawn on a mirror, and beyond them a rounded, rocky dome of a mountain stood in front of layers of blue ridges. It was just the opening act.

The main act came about a quarter hour later, once the sun had slipped behind the ridge. High streaks of cirrus, miles above the lake, were still catching sunlight that no longer reached the ground, so they glowed orange and gold while the water and the forest sank into shade. Don't leave when the sun does. That's when the clouds do their best work. The buoys went from red to nearly black, and the lake soaked up the sky's colors. I filmed it in short phone clips, so the frames below are stills pulled from video and a little soft. The color was gone within minutes, but the lake kept it a little longer than the sky did.
